battle.title: AI PR Reviewer for OSS Repos
battle.idea: An AI agent that reviews pull requests on open-source repositories, catches subtle bugs, style violations, and missing tests before a human maintainer ever looks at the diff.

brief.goal: Build an AI agent that performs first-pass review on pull requests for OSS maintainers, reducing triage backlog by surfacing clear bugs, missing tests, and style issues.
constraints: GitHub App with read-only scope by default
Comments posted within 90s of PR open
No shell execution on reviewed repo
Handle repos up to 100k stars with rate-limit awareness
brief.targetUser: OSS maintainers who triage 20+ PRs per week and want to skip clear rejections
successCriteria: >=70% of posted comments accepted by maintainer
Zero false positives on skipped tests

teams.name: Safe Builders
teams.strategy: Conservative GitHub App with read-only scope, cites every claim, declines to comment when confidence is low.

teams.name: Viral Designers
teams.strategy: Personality-driven reviewer with meme comments, leaderboard, and public badge for top-reviewed PRs.

teams.name: Infra Hackers
teams.strategy: Self-hosted runner with AST-level analysis, custom linter integration, and webhook-first architecture.

proposals.oneLiner: A cautious AI reviewer that only comments when it is certain, and cites its evidence.
proposals.targetUser: OSS maintainers burned by noisy bots
proposals.problem: Existing PR-review bots flood maintainers with low-signal comments.
proposals.solution: Read-only GitHub App that posts comments only on high-confidence findings with file:line citations.
proposals.demoPlan: Open a PR with 3 seeded bugs; show 3 inline comments and silence on 5 minor style nits.
proposals.technicalHighlight: RAG over CONTRIBUTING.md and past accepted reviews to calibrate style per repo.
risks: Over-cautious threshold may miss real bugs
GitHub App approval flow is friction
proposals.whyThisCanWin: Trust is the moat: maintainers install a bot that proves it knows when not to speak.

proposals.oneLiner: A sarcastic AI reviewer with a public leaderboard and weekly trophy for the worst-diff PR.
proposals.targetUser: OSS contributors who want feedback that feels human
proposals.problem: OSS contribution is lonely; feedback is sterile.
proposals.solution: AI reviewer with witty persona, public leaderboard, weekly trophies for clean PRs.
proposals.demoPlan: Submit 3 PRs from clean to sloppy; show escalating persona reactions and trophy on the clean one.
proposals.technicalHighlight: Persona-conditioned generation with sentiment-aware tone clamping.
proposals.whyThisCanWin: Viral loop: contributors share review cards, bringing new users.

proposals.oneLiner: A self-hosted PR reviewer that runs AST analysis and custom linters before any LLM call.
proposals.targetUser: Platform teams that cannot send code to external APIs
proposals.problem: Cloud-only AI reviewers violate data-residency and miss deep code-structure signals.
proposals.solution: Self-hosted reviewer: webhook triggers AST diff and custom linters, then LLM summarises flagged spans only.
mvpFeatures: AST diff for TypeScript, Python, Go
LLM invoked only on flagged spans
proposals.demoPlan: Run Helm chart locally; submit PR; show AST tree, linter findings, LLM summary on top span.
proposals.technicalHighlight: AST pre-filter cuts LLM tokens by 80% and keeps code on customer infrastructure.
risks: AST limited to 3 languages at MVP
proposals.whyThisCanWin: Enterprise procurement teams pay for the only reviewer that respects their data boundary.

attacks.claim: ReviewGuard cite-to-line is table stakes; Copilot, CodeRabbit, Sourcery all do it.
attacks.evidence: All three incumbents post file:line comments. PRD names no unique angle beyond caution.
attacks.suggestedFix: Add per-author style history and quantify noise reduction vs incumbents.

attacks.claim: Demo only shows 3 of 8 candidates; the silence claim needs precision/recall.
attacks.evidence: Demo script does not report precision/recall vs CodeRabbit on same PR set.
attacks.suggestedFix: Add 50-PR benchmark with precision/recall before claiming the silence.

attacks.claim: Persona-conditioned tone clamping is unsolved; strict CoC repos will ban the bot.
attacks.evidence: 2024 snark-bot incidents led to repo bans within days; no CoC-aware override described.
attacks.suggestedFix: Detect CODEOWNERS and CoC files; degrade to neutral persona automatically.

attacks.claim: Leaderboards on private corporate repos are a non-feature.
attacks.evidence: Proposal targets OSS contributors but leaderboard assumes public-by-default visibility.
attacks.suggestedFix: Split into two SKUs: public leaderboard for OSS, opt-in private dashboard for enterprise.

attacks.claim: Self-hosted Helm chart plus AST pipeline plus pluggable linters is 6 months of work, not 48h.
attacks.evidence: Single-language AST diff with backpressure is multi-week; no scoping to MVP language.
attacks.suggestedFix: Scope MVP to TypeScript only with eslint; defer Python and Go to v0.2.

attacks.claim: Enterprise data-residency buyers prefer Sonar or Snyk; a 48h team cannot displace them.
attacks.evidence: Fortune 500 procurement cycles are 6-12 months; no anchor customer named.
attacks.suggestedFix: Pivot to mid-market (50-500 devs) where procurement is faster and pain is acute.

defenses.responseToAttack: Cite-to-line is table stakes only for cloud bots with write scope; not for read-only Apps. Unique angle is confidence-gated silence plus per-repo style RAG.
defenses.revision: Added explicit comparison vs CodeRabbit and Sourcery on signal-to-noise.

defenses.responseToAttack: Accepted: the 3-of-8 demo is anecdotal. We will add a 50-PR benchmark with precision/recall vs CodeRabbit before launch.
defenses.revision: Benchmark section added to demo_script; results required before GA.

defenses.responseToAttack: Rejected in scope: persona clamping plus CODEOWNERS detection will ship in v0.2; CoC override is already in the PRD.
defenses.revision: No code change; persona override already tracked as P1 in PRD.

defenses.responseToAttack: Accepted: private dashboard for enterprise is implicit but not stated; will add explicitly.
defenses.revision: Positioning split into OSS (public leaderboard) and Enterprise (private dashboard) added to pitch_outline.

defenses.responseToAttack: Accepted partially: scope MVP to TypeScript with eslint only, defer Python and Go to v0.2.
defenses.revision: MVP scope narrowed to TypeScript + eslint; Python and Go moved to v0.2.

defenses.responseToAttack: Accepted: Fortune 500 procurement is out of scope. Mid-market positioning adopted.
defenses.revision: Target user updated to mid-market platform teams (50-500 engineers).

judgeComments: Trust-first positioning is the right bet for the user.
48h scope is realistic; MVP is shippable.
scores.winningReason: Highest userValue and feasibility scores; trust is the right moat.

judgeComments: Persona idea is fresh and demoable.
Viral loop plausible but depends on OSS adoption.
scores.losingReason: Persona risk and enterprise unaddressed cost it feasibility and userValue.

judgeComments: Technical depth is strongest of three.
scores.losingReason: Scope too broad for time budget; market moves slowly.

artifacts.title: ReviewGuard Product Brief
artifacts.content:
# ReviewGuard

## Problem
OSS maintainers are overwhelmed by noisy PR-review bots that post low-signal comments.

## Solution
A read-only GitHub App that posts inline comments only on high-confidence findings, each backed by a file:line citation. When confidence is below threshold, the bot stays silent.

## Target User
OSS maintainers triaging 20+ PRs per week.

## Success Metric
>=70% of posted comments accepted (thumbs-up) by the maintainer within 7 days.

artifacts.title: ReviewGuard PRD
artifacts.content:
# ReviewGuard PRD v0.1

## Goals
1. Post high-confidence cited comments within 90s of PR open.
2. Stay silent on low-confidence spans.
3. Ship a GitHub App installable in two clicks with read-only scope.

## Requirements
- R1: GitHub App with read-only default scope.
- R2: Confidence threshold configurable per repo (default 0.85).
- R3: Per-comment citation to file:line.
- R4: Dry-run preview mode.
- R5: Repo-level mute toggle.

## Open Questions
- Monorepos with multiple CONTRIBUTING.md?
- Cold-start calibration from per-repo past-review data?

artifacts.title: ReviewGuard Architecture
artifacts.content:
# ReviewGuard Architecture

## Components
- Webhook receiver: accepts PR events, validates signature.
- Diff parser: extracts changed hunks with file:line ranges.
- Style RAG: retrieves CONTRIBUTING.md and recent accepted reviews.
- Comment scorer: assigns confidence to candidate comments.
- Comment poster: posts only comments above threshold.

## Latency Budget
- Webhook to parsed diff: 2s
- Style RAG: 5s
- Comment scoring: 20s
- Post: 3s
- Total: 30s p50, 60s p95

# AI PR Reviewer for OSS Repos - Battle Export

**Battle ID**: btl_hack001
**Status**: completed
**Winner**: team_safe_v1 (Safe Builders)

## Brief
Build an AI agent that performs first-pass review on pull requests for OSS maintainers, reducing triage backlog.

## Teams
- **Safe Builders** (safe, 52.2): ReviewGuard - read-only GitHub App with cited comments.
- **Viral Designers** (aggressive, 47.8): RoastMyPR - persona-driven reviewer with leaderboard.
- **Infra Hackers** (balanced, 49.5): ASTReview - self-hosted AST-aware reviewer.

## Outcome
Safe Builders wins on userValue (9.0) and feasibility (9.0). Viral Designers scores highest on novelty (8.5) and demoWow (8.5). Infra Hackers leads on technical depth (9.0).
